body: I didn't screen by theme. I looked for the Radico 2016-17 / Motilal Oswal "twin engine" setup: a step-change in OPM and ROCE lasting several quarters, debt falling, no equity dilution, self-funded capex, no promoter pledge (ideally promoter buying), FII/DII holdings rising for several quarters in a row, market cap ₹300-10,000 cr and P/E of about 30 or less.
title: quant_pattern_hunt › Stage 1: Context (theme-agnostic)

body:
| Claim in the brief | What I found | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Record SIP flows of ~₹31–32k cr/month | Sep 2026 SIP flows set a record at ₹32,490 cr. Oct 2026 was **₹32,160 cr (−1% MoM)**. Equity MF inflows fell **14% MoM** to ₹32,994 cr in Oct. SIP AUM ₹17.68 lakh cr; ~10 cr contributing accounts (AMFI data via Kotak Neo / 5paisa, 11 Nov 2026) | **Confirmed, but momentum has plateaued** |
| RBI rate cuts in 2025 | 125 bp of cuts in 2025 (Feb, Apr, Jun 50 bp, Dec). Repo held at **5.25%** at the Feb, Apr, Jun and Aug 2026 meetings. RBI flagged an oil shock / West Asia conflict and rupee weakness. I could not confirm the Oct 2026 decision | Confirmed. **No further easing in 2026, and the inflation risk now points up** |
| GST 2.0 (22 Sep 2025) | FMCG volumes were *soft* right after the change: NIQ Oct–Dec 2025 value +7.8%, volume +2.6%, held back by transition and a high base. ICRA says sales growth improved in Q3 FY26. Q2 FY27 (Sep-26 qtr) prints are strong at Nestle, Honasa, Bajaj Consumer, Radico and Mrs Bectors | Confirmed with a lag. The demand revival is showing up in FY27 numbers |
| Income-tax cut, Budget 2025 | ₹12 lakh zero-tax threshold, effective FY26. Taken from prior knowledge; **not re-verified this session** | Assumed |
| STT hike on F&O from 1 Apr 2026 | Futures 0.02%→0.05%, options 0.10%→0.15% of premium (Business Today, 26–27 Mar 2026). Forecasts ranged from −20–30% volumes to "limited impact". **I found no clean post-April volume data** | Confirmed as policy. The impact is unquantified |

**Thesis in two sentences.** Household savings are still moving into equities through SIPs at about ₹32k cr a month, but that flow has stopped accelerating. The money is in companies whose earnings grow with the *AUM stock* rather than with *trading turnover*. On consumption, real income relief (tax cuts plus GST 2.0) began showing up in volumes from mid-2026, so the best setups are companies where revenue growth comes *together with* a mix or operating-leverage margin step-change, not ones where price is doing all the work.

**Second-order check on the "F&O losers".** The loser trade looks **already played out in the reported numbers**. Angel One's Sep-26 quarter PAT was ₹335 cr vs ₹212 cr YoY, with OPM at 45%. CDSL's Sep-26 quarter PAT was ₹173 cr vs ₹140 cr. A short or avoid call based purely on the STT hike is stale. Angel One is still avoided, for its balance sheet: borrowings ₹7,632 cr and CFO of −₹4,142 cr in FY26.

body:
- **id:** `thesis:paper-call:US-PG:q2fy27-organic-sales-3pct-plus`
- **Method:** management-tone-vs-delivery · **P(ours)** 0.45 · **P(base)** 0.40 · resolve by 2027-01-31
- **Evidence:** Q1 FY27 release (22-Oct-2026): net sales $23.3bn (+4%), organic +4% (volume +2, mix +1, price minor) — above the maintained FY27 organic guide of 1–3% (incl. 30–50 bps headwind from discontinuations); FY27 core EPS guide $6.89–7.11 (in-line to +3%) maintained; CEO Jejurikar: 'we expect there will continue to be geopolitical and economic challenges'; Thorne acquired 1-Oct-2026 (excluded from organic).
- **Why our number differs from base:** Management-tone test: P&G kept its full-year range after a quarter well above it and talked down the macro; the gap between cautious words and a volume-led +4% suggests momentum management is not yet willing to bank. Against that, comparisons and the discontinuation headwind weigh. We nudge above the base.
- **Base-rate reasoning:** Naive: with full-year guidance of 1–3%, a quarter at ≥3% is the upper end; P&G printed ≥3% organic in roughly 4 of the last 10 quarters (from memory, unverified) → ~40%.
- **Resolution rule:** YES if P&G's reported organic sales growth for the quarter ended 31-Dec-2026 (Q2 FY27 earnings release) is ≥3% (as rounded by the company).
- **Resolution source:** P&G Q2 FY27 earnings release (8-K, EDGAR; pginvestor.com)
- **Sources used:** https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/80424/000008042426000250/fy2627q1jas8-kexhibit991.htm
- **Confidence of evidence:** single-source

title: batch2 › 30. PG — Procter & Gamble reports Q2 FY27 (Oct–Dec 2026) organic sales growth ≥3%

body:
- Every scored promise was met or beaten (12 of 12): FY2025 organic flat to +3% (Aug) -> +5%; reported +2-5% -> +8.4% (XBRL); adjusted operating margin +50-110 bp -> +190 bp; FCF conversion >=100% -> 104.5% (XBRL re-derived); every next-quarter organic and margin band beaten (Q3-25 organic +9% vs 2-5%; Q1-26 +12% vs 4-8%; Q2-26 +12.2% vs 4-8%).
- This is the profile of a **systematic sandbagger**: guidance was raised at every call in 2025-26 (FY2026 organic 2-6% -> 8-11% -> 11-12%). A 100% delivery record is evidence of conservative guiding, not of foresight. Data-centre demand (now high-single-digit % of sales) drove most of the 2026 beats.
- Pending FY2026: organic 11-12%, reported 17-18%, adjusted operating margin 20.3-20.4%, FCF conversion >=90%, Q4 organic 9-12%. These are now one-quarter-ahead guides, so delivery should be high again.
- The rule still gives WTS only P = 0.47 on its two FY2026 growth calls, because the peers' strict revenue/growth delivery is low (41%, dragged by A. O. Smith's China and water-treatment misses) and the shrink weight is 0.375. This is the case where 'company credibility' (very high) and 'sector base rate' (low) disagree most: a good test of the shrink.
